worst_places.before: `node16` reflects real Node.js ESM behavior: requires explicit extensions in relative imports (`./utils.js`); TypeScript finds `utils.ts` when it sees the import `"./utils.js"`. `bundler` is designed for projects with webpack/vite/esbuild: extensions are optional (the bundler handles resolution), supports `package.json` exports. `bundler` is more convenient for frontend — no need to write `.js` extensions in TypeScript imports. `node16` is required for publishing ESM libraries under Node.js.
worst_places.after:
`node16` copies what Node.js really does with ES modules (ESM). Relative imports must carry an extension, and it must be `.js`:

```ts
import { foo } from "./utils";    // ❌ ESM needs the extension
import { foo } from "./utils.js"; // ✅ TypeScript still reads utils.ts
```

`bundler` is for projects where webpack, vite or esbuild resolves imports. Extensions are optional there, because the bundler finds the file. Both strategies read the `exports` map in `package.json`.

Pick `bundler` for frontend: you never write `.js` in a TypeScript import. Pick `node16` when you publish an ESM library for Node.js.

patterns: POSITIVE MODEL — articles 01-10 run a fixed five-beat rhythm that is the single best structural habit found anywhere on the site, and it is why flag density here is 7.0/1k, the lowest of any zone: (1) an H2 whose first sentence is a one-line plain-language definition with no warm-up ('Условный тип — это выражение уровня типов, которое работает как тернарный оператор'); (2) an ASCII ```txt``` box that shows the shape before any prose expands it; (3) a ❌-then-✅ code pair — the wrong way first, then the fix, in the SAME block; (4) the real compiler diagnostic pasted as an inline comment on the offending line, never paraphrased ('Duplicate identifier 'Point'', 'Object literal may only specify known properties', 'Type instantiation is excessively deep', 'Expression produces a union type that is too complex to represent', 'Object is possibly 'undefined''), ~41 verbatim diagnostics across the 11 EN files; (5) a closing 'Типичные ошибки на интервью' / 'Common Interview Traps' section of 6-7 bullets, each shaped as quoted-misconception-then-correction. This is the same discipline that made question-bank q-1..q-44 the best material on the site, and it holds for all ten teaching articles instead of dropping halfway. It also keeps code blocks at one per ~90 words, so no idea travels more than a screen without something concrete to hold.

THE SEAM IS BY GENRE, NOT BY POSITION — articles 01-10 are uniformly excellent (RU 01, 02, 06, 08, 09, 10 have literally zero long sentences), and every mechanical flag in the zone concentrates in file 11, the Q&A article: 11 theory walls, 17 long paragraphs, 21 over-limit sentences in EN (7.1%) against 0-3 in every other file. The cause is measurable: file 11 carries 4146 words on 17 code blocks (one per ~244 words) while articles 01-10 average one per ~90 words. Beat (2) of the rhythm — the ```txt``` box — disappears entirely, and beats (3) and (4) survive only occasionally. File 11 is also the only file in the zone with no `<!-- verified: 2026-06-23 -->` header, suggesting it never went through the same review pass. Fixing it does not need new content, only the existing eight-flag list, the node16/bundler comparison and the isolatedModules answer converted into the ```txt``` boxes and ❌/✅ pairs that article 10 already contains.

THE QUIZ BANK IS NOT WRITTEN TO THE SAME STANDARD AS ANYTHING ELSE IN THE ZONE, AND FIVE ITEMS ARE FACTUALLY BROKEN — quiz-20 contradicts articles 01 and 02 on unconstrained generic widening (and contradicts quiz-32, which uses the same function); quiz-25 asserts `true | false` differs from `boolean`, contradicting article 03; quiz-29's explanation states and then denies the same conclusion two sentences apart and its marked answer matches neither; quiz-30's explanation concedes that its own distractor D is also correct, contradicting article 10's list of eight strict flags; quiz-28's marked-correct option is captioned with the reason it is wrong. None of these would survive the articles' review bar. Separately, the bank quotes real compiler output only twice (quiz-14 'Cannot assign to 'name' because it is a readonly property', quiz-40 'Argument of type 'string | null' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'') — the habit that makes the articles trustworthy is almost entirely absent here.

ANSWER-SHAPE TELLS — correctIndex is not distributed: index 0 is correct in 26 of 38 items (68.4%), index 1 in 10, index 2 in 2, and index 3 is NEVER correct (0 of 38; expected ~9.5 each). A reader who notices this can score ~68% without reading the questions, and can eliminate the last option in every single item for free. Option length leaks the same way: the correct option is the strictly longest in 18/38 EN items (47.4%, plus 3 tied at longest = 21/38 at-or-tied) and 15/38 RU (39.5%, plus 2 tied); mean correct-option length is 61.4 chars against 47.8 for distractors in EN (+28%) and 63.9 vs 52.1 in RU (+23%). The tell is caused by a habit: the correct option is written as a full explanatory clause ('Interfaces support declaration merging, while type aliases do not') while distractors are stubs ('Type aliases are faster at runtime than interfaces').

THE QUIZ REPEATS ITSELF INSTEAD OF COVERING THE ARTICLES — seven of 38 items (quiz-1, 6, 11, 21, 26, 31, 36 — 18%) ask the identical `interface` vs `type` declaration-merging fact, several with near-identical stems and explanations; add quiz-16 and it is 21% of the bank on one paragraph of article 01.
